title: Policy evaluation pipeline refactor for multi-level region/tier selection and model-variant fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Refactor the policy evaluation pipeline to introduce a typed selector intermediate representation (IR) that cleanly separates syntax validation from runtime decision logic. Goal: support multi-level selection (region shards -> tier routing -> weighted variants) with deterministic fallback ordering, stricter schema checks, and a compatibility shim so older configs continue to run. Primary motivation comes from recent incidents where cascading fallbacks produced non-deterministic region choices under load and where ad-hoc rule priorities made rollouts unreliable. This ticket implements the compiler and validator stages, the runtime contract for the IR, and the migration tools to convert v1 routing rules to the new typed selector format.
acceptance_criteria: New typed selector IR produced by compiler with stable JSON schema and version field (selector_v2).
DSL compiler performs 4 staged validations: schema lint -> static type check -> semantic conflict detector -> canonicalizer.
Runtime accepts selector_v1 (via shim) and selector_v2; selector_v2 exercised by default in canary namespace behind feature flag.
Deterministic fallback ordering for variant selection (region -> tier -> variant) documented and validated by unit+integration tests.
Console shows validation diagnostics per-policy with link to failing rule and suggested fix.
End-to-end benchmarks show <=5% median latency regression at 95th percentile for policy evaluation path under 10k RPS workload compared to baseline.
Migration tool supports batch conversion of existing policy bundles with a dry-run mode and a commit step.
Backward compatibility tests (policy roundtrip) pass for 95% of historical policies in orgs with heavy fallback usage.
design_decisions: Introduce typed selector IR instead of embedding complex semantics in raw DSL. This reduces runtime branching and simplifies formal validation.
Keep the DSL surface backwards-compatible but mark deprecated constructs; compiler emits warnings with suggested rewrites.
Separate validator into two processes: pre-commit (fast lint + type checks) and pre-deploy (semantic conflict detection requiring model catalog/lookups).
Use deterministic stable sorting for tie-breakers: explicit priority -> tier weight -> lexicographic region id to avoid non-determinism observed previously.
Expose a feature flag policy.refactor.v2 for progressive rollout rather than a global switch.
Console-facing diagnostics include exact snippet and byte offsets to reduce triage time for PMs and customers.
migration_plan: Phase 0: Add selector_v2 schema and compatibility shim to runtime; publish compiler in alpha.
Phase 1 (canary): Convert 10 internal and 2 customer policies using dry-run; compare eval traces and fallbacks.
Phase 2 (gradual): Offer automated conversion in Console with preview and rollback; run nightly batch conversions for low-risk orgs.
Phase 3 (opt-in default): Switch new policies created in Console to v2; keep v1 runtime shim for 6 months before deprecation.
Provide a migration checklist and a one-click revert in Console for converted policies.
test_plan: Unit tests for compiler stages (schema, type, semantic) with 600+ synthetic DSL permutations.
Property tests that assert selector_v2 roundtrips to equivalent runtime decisions as selector_v1 for converted policies.
Integration tests with model catalog mock to validate variant compatibility and fallback ordering.
Load tests at 10k RPS and 95th percentile token-generation concurrency to measure CPU and latency impact.
Chaos test: inject region weight spikes and validate graceful fallback without request loss or increased error-rate >0.5%.
E2E Canary runs in dedicated namespace with telemetry: policy-eval latency, error-rate, fallback count per request.
rollout_plan: Deploy compiler and validator to staging; run full conversion of internal policies to catch edge-cases.
Enable feature flag for team namespace A (canary) for 72 hours and monitor errors and fallback traces.
If stable, expand to 10% of orgs with low traffic, run validation and additional load tests.
Expose migration UI in Console behind a 'Try v2' toggle; allow customers to opt-in.
Schedule deprecation announcement 60 days before recommended v1 removal.
notes: We deliberately do not change runtime routing heuristics (batching, KV cache) in this ticket — only policy evaluation flow.
This work should reduce future complexity for region-aware autoscaling policies by canonicalizing selector logic.
Potential perf hotspot: semantic checks that consult model capability matrix — cached aggressively and rate-limited.
We will add telemetry tags: policy_compiler_version, selector_version, conversion_dryrun=true/false.
comments: 2026-02-14 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after postmortem on region fallback incident. Attached diagnosis notes.

2026-02-20 - Marcus Lee: Spike completed evaluating IR shapes. Two viable IR candidates: flow-tree and flat-typed selector. Chosen flat-typed selector for smaller memory footprint and simpler canonicalization.
2026-02-28 - Marcus Lee: Prototype compiler stage-1 ready (schema lint + type checks). Found ~4% of org policies use deprecated 'preferred_zone' field; added auto-warn rule.
2026-03-03 - Design review (Priya Kumar): Console diagnostics UX approved; suggested inline example fixes instead of only warnings.

2026-03-07 - Eng review (Kenji Watanabe): Benchmarks show 8% p95 regression in naive implementation; optimized tie-break path to reduce to 3.6% p95. Need further reduction to meet acceptance criterion.

2026-03-10 - Marcus Lee: Added compatibility shim to runtime; basic roundtrip conversion passes against 80% of sampled policies. Remaining failures are complex regex-based region selectors — task created to augment compiler regex handling.
2026-03-12 - QA (Emily Zhang): First integration smoke tests passed in canary namespace. Noted one flaky test related to model catalog staleness — added cache warmup in pre-deploy checks.
